column1: # Mutants no test can tell from the original, by set. Tab-separated:
#   <set>  <manifest key>  <site>  <why no test can observe the mutation>
# The site fingerprints the whole function the mutation sits in, and where in
# it the mutation starts (`borzoi_oracle_harness::mutants::site_of`): a key's
# ` #<n>` passes to another mutant when one with the same description is added
# before it, and an edit to the function, its signature included, may make the
# mutation observable, so either fails the row until it is reviewed. An
# argument that leans on code outside the function (a type's definition, a
# caller) must say so, and is the reviewer's to re-check when that moves. `mutants-manifest` prints the site a
# row's key has now, so a new row can start from a placeholder.
# The reason is an argument that the mutated program behaves identically on
# every input, not that no test checks it today: a mutant only a missing test
# would catch is a survivor to kill, not an entry here. A row whose mutant the
# run caught, or that names no mutant of its set, fails `mutants-manifest`.
